Definition: opening (of a dungeon), i.e. jail-delivery (figuratively, salvation for sin)
BiblicalUsage: Peqach-qowach is the opening of the prison, jail-delivery. Isaiah says the Spirit anointed him to proclaim liberty to the captives and the opening of the prison to those who are bound — the verse Jesus read in the synagogue and said was fulfilled that day.
TheologicalSignificance: I am convinced that the opening of the prison is the gospel itself: Christ came to loose the bound, and the doors He opens no man shuts.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
